```{=html}
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@supabase/supabase-js@2"></script>
<script>
const SUPABASE_URL = 'https://hpyezixseggwnrpepbhx.supabase.co';
const SUPABASE_KEY = 'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJzdXBhYmFzZSIsInJlZiI6ImhweWV6aXhzZWdnd25ycGVwYmh4Iiwicm9sZSI6ImFub24iLCJpYXQiOjE3NzY4MTUzMDgsImV4cCI6MjA5MjM5MTMwOH0.HGcrv7-I07yFES2qBRhXf1j3UCbfMb8PwlWkQjY6NYs';
let sbClient;
let _initialized = false;

(function waitForSupabase() {
  if (typeof supabase === 'undefined') return setTimeout(waitForSupabase, 100);
  if (_initialized) return;
  _initialized = true;

  sbClient = supabase.createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_KEY, {
    auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false, detectSessionInUrl: true }
  });

  const savedSession = sessionStorage.getItem('sb-session');
  if (savedSession) sbClient.auth.setSession(JSON.parse(savedSession));

  sbClient.auth.onAuthStateChange(async (event, session) => {
    if (event === 'SIGNED_IN' || event === 'TOKEN_REFRESHED') {
      if (session) sessionStorage.setItem('sb-session', JSON.stringify(session));
      if (window.location.hash.includes('access_token'))
        window.history.replaceState({}, document.title, window.location.pathname);
      updateWeekBar();
    }
    if (event === 'SIGNED_OUT') {
      sessionStorage.removeItem('sb-session');
      updateWeekBar();
    }
  });

  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => setTimeout(updateWeekBar, 300));
  } else {
    setTimeout(updateWeekBar, 300);
  }
})();

var W2_CHUNK_COUNT = 20;
var W2_QUIZ_IDS = ['w2_q_loading', 'w2_q_cleanup', 'w2_q_viz', 'w2_q_exercises'];

function getLang() {
  try { return localStorage.getItem('da_course_lang') || 'python'; } catch(e){ return 'python'; }
}

async function sbSaveProgress(key, value) {
  localStorage.setItem(key, value);
  try {
    const savedSession = sessionStorage.getItem('sb-session');
    const user = savedSession ? JSON.parse(savedSession).user : null;
    if (user && sbClient) {
      const { error } = await sbClient.from('progress').upsert({ id: user.id, key: key, value: value });
      if (error) console.error("Supabase Error:", error.message);
    }
  } catch (err) { console.error("System Error:", err); }
}

async function markChunkDone(chunkId) {
  const key = 'chunk_' + getLang() + '_' + chunkId;
  await sbSaveProgress(key, 'true');
  updateWeekBar();
}

async function markQuizDone(quizId) {
  const key = 'quiz_' + getLang() + '_w2_' + quizId;
  await sbSaveProgress(key, 'true');
  updateWeekBar();
}

async function updateWeekBar() {
  var lang = getLang();
  var total = W2_CHUNK_COUNT + W2_QUIZ_IDS.length;
  var done = 0;
  try {
    const savedSession = sessionStorage.getItem('sb-session');
    const user = savedSession ? JSON.parse(savedSession).user : null;
    let progressMap = {};
    if (user && sbClient) {
      const { data } = await sbClient.from('progress').select('key, value').eq('id', user.id);
      if (data) data.forEach(row => { progressMap[row.key] = row.value === 'true'; });
    }
    const isDone = (key) => progressMap[key] === true || localStorage.getItem(key) === 'true';
    for (var i = 1; i <= W2_CHUNK_COUNT; i++) {
      if (isDone('chunk_' + lang + '_w2_c' + i)) done++;
    }
    W2_QUIZ_IDS.forEach(id => {
      if (isDone('quiz_' + lang + '_w2_' + id)) done++;
    });
    var pct = Math.round((done / total) * 100);
    var bar = document.getElementById('week2-progress-bar');
    var txt = document.getElementById('week2-progress-text');
    if (bar) { bar.style.width = pct + '%'; bar.innerText = pct > 8 ? pct + '%' : ''; }
    if (txt) { txt.innerText = done + ' of ' + total + ' tasks completed (' + lang.toUpperCase() + ')'; }
  } catch (err) { console.error("Update Bar Error:", err); }
}

var _observedChunks = {};

function resetObservers() {
  _observedChunks = {};
  setTimeout(scanChunkWrappers, 300);
}

function observeChunkWrapper(wrapper) {
  var chunkId = wrapper.getAttribute('data-chunk-id');
  if (!chunkId || _observedChunks[chunkId]) return;
  _observedChunks[chunkId] = true;

  function tryAttach() {
    var iframe = wrapper.querySelector('iframe');
    if (!iframe) { setTimeout(tryAttach, 500); return; }
    function tryObserve() {
      try {
        var doc = iframe.contentDocument || iframe.contentWindow.document;
        if (!doc || !doc.body || doc.body.innerHTML.trim() === '') {
          setTimeout(tryObserve, 600); return;
        }
        var obs = new MutationObserver(function() {
          try {
            var pres = doc.querySelectorAll('pre');
            var hasOutput = false;
            pres.forEach(function(p) { if (p.innerText && p.innerText.trim()) hasOutput = true; });
            if (hasOutput) { obs.disconnect(); markChunkDone(chunkId); }
          } catch(e) {}
        });
        obs.observe(doc.body, { childList: true, subtree: true, characterData: true });
      } catch(e) { setTimeout(tryObserve, 800); }
    }
    tryObserve();
  }
  tryAttach();
}

function scanChunkWrappers() {
  document.querySelectorAll('.chunk-track[data-chunk-id]').forEach(observeChunkWrapper);
}

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  setTimeout(scanChunkWrappers, 500);
  setTimeout(scanChunkWrappers, 2000);
  new MutationObserver(function(muts) {
    let found = false;
    muts.forEach(m => {
      m.addedNodes.forEach(n => {
        if (n.nodeType === 1 && (n.classList?.contains('chunk-track') || n.querySelector?.('.chunk-track'))) found = true;
      });
    });
    if (found) setTimeout(scanChunkWrappers, 300);
  }).observe(document.body, { childList: true, subtree: true });
});

window.addEventListener('message', function(e) {
  if (e.data && e.data.type === 'chunkDone' && e.data.chunkId) markChunkDone(e.data.chunkId);
});

// Language Switcher
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  function applyFinalStyle() {
    var links = document.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav .nav-link');
    var pyBtn, rBtn;
    links.forEach(function(l) {
      if (l.textContent.trim() === 'PYTHON') pyBtn = l;
      if (l.textContent.trim() === 'R') rBtn = l;
    });
    if (!pyBtn || !rBtn) { setTimeout(applyFinalStyle, 200); return; }
    var dg = '#1a4d1a';
    function updateView(lang) {
      document.querySelectorAll('.lang-python').forEach(function(el){ el.style.display = lang==='python'?'block':'none'; });
      document.querySelectorAll('.lang-r').forEach(function(el){ el.style.display = lang==='r'?'block':'none'; });
      pyBtn.style.cssText = 'background-color:'+(lang==='python'?dg:'white')+' !important;color:'+(lang==='python'?'white':dg)+' !important;border:2px solid '+dg+' !important;border-radius:50px !important;padding:5px 20px !important;margin:5px !important;font-weight:800 !important;';
      rBtn.style.cssText  = 'background-color:'+(lang==='r'?dg:'white')+' !important;color:'+(lang==='r'?'white':dg)+' !important;border:2px solid '+dg+' !important;border-radius:50px !important;padding:5px 20px !important;margin:5px !important;font-weight:800 !important;';
      try { localStorage.setItem('da_course_lang', lang); } catch(e){}
      updateWeekBar();
      resetObservers();
    }
    pyBtn.addEventListener('click', function(e){ e.preventDefault(); updateView('python'); });
    rBtn.addEventListener('click', function(e){ e.preventDefault(); updateView('r'); });
    var saved = localStorage.getItem('da_course_lang') || 'python';
    updateView(saved);
  }
  applyFinalStyle();
});
window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => {
  sessionStorage.setItem('needs-refresh', 'true');
});
</script>
```

## 1 – Loading and Exploring Data

When you receive a dataset for the first time, your first goal is to **understand its structure** before doing any analysis.

### `head()` and `tail()` — your first look

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c1">
```
```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 310
library(shiny)
CHUNK_ID <- "w2_c1"
DAT <- data.frame(
  age    = c(46, 29, 58, 67, 64, 34, 30, 37),
  gender = c("female","female","female","male","male","female","male","male"),
  chol   = c(203, 165, 228, 259, 294, 155, 170, 205),
  weight = c(202, 122, 165, 189, 170, 125, 143, 156),
  bp.2s  = as.numeric(rep(NA, 8)),
  location = c("Louisa","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa")
)
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
  textAreaInput("code", "head() / tail()", value = "head(dat)      # First 6 rows (default)\nhead(dat, 3)   # First 3 rows\ntail(dat, 2)   # Last 2 rows", width = '100%', height = '80px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),
  verbatimTextOutput("out")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$run, {
    session$sendCustomMessage("chunkRun", list(chunkId = CHUNK_ID))
    output$out <- renderPrint({
      dat <- DAT
      exprs <- parse(text = input$code)
      for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) }
    })
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```
```{=html}
</div>
```

### `summary()` — a full statistical overview

`summary()` is one of the most useful first steps: it shows **min, quartiles, mean, median, max** for numeric columns, and **counts** for categorical columns. It also reveals how many `NA` values exist in each column.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c4">
```
```{shinylive-r}

#| viewerHeight: 340

CHUNK_ID <- "w2_c4"
DAT <- data.frame(
  age    = c(46, 29, 58, 67, 64, 34, 30, 37),
  gender = c("female","female","female","male","male","female","male","male"),
  chol   = c(203, 165, 228, 259, 294, 155, 170, 205),
  glyhb  = c(4.31, 4.86, 5.06, 5.40, 11.93, NA, 5.12, 4.95)
)
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
  textAreaInput("code", "summary()", value = "summary(dat)   # Notice the NA's count in glyhb!", width = '100%', height = '50px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),
  verbatimTextOutput("out")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$run, {
    session$sendCustomMessage("chunkRun", list(chunkId = CHUNK_ID))
    output$out <- renderPrint({
      dat <- DAT
      exprs <- parse(text = input$code)
      for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) }
    })
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

## 2 – Data Cleanup

Raw data is rarely analysis-ready. You typically need to remove irrelevant columns, handle missing values (`NA`), and reorder variables. Four functions are essential for this:  `which()`, `%in%`, `is.na()`, and `apply()`.

### `which()` — finding positions

`which()` returns the **indices** (positions) of elements where a condition is `TRUE` — not the values themselves.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c7">
```
```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 240
library(shiny)
CHUNK_ID <- "w2_c7"
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
  textAreaInput("code", "which()", value = "x <- c(10, 3, 7, 15, 2, 8)\nwhich(x > 5)     # Positions where condition is TRUE\nwhich.min(x)     # Position of smallest value\nwhich.max(x)     # Position of largest value\nx[which(x > 5)]  # The actual values at those positions", width = '100%', height = '120px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),
  verbatimTextOutput("out")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$run, {
    session$sendCustomMessage("chunkRun", list(chunkId = CHUNK_ID))
    output$out <- renderPrint({
      exprs <- parse(text = input$code)
      for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) }
    })
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```
```{=html}
</div>
```

### `%in%` — testing membership

`%in%` checks whether each element of one vector appears in a second vector. Combined with `which()`, it is the standard way to find columns by name.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c8">
```
```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 260

CHUNK_ID <- "w2_c8"
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
  textAreaInput("code", "%in%", value = "fruits <- c('apple', 'banana', 'cherry', 'date')\nfruits %in% c('banana', 'date')         # Logical vector\nwhich(fruits %in% c('banana', 'date'))  # Positions\n\n# Practical: find column indices to remove\ncols <- c('age', 'bp.2s', 'chol', 'time.ppn')\nwhich(cols %in% c('bp.2s', 'time.ppn'))", width = '100%', height = '130px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),
  verbatimTextOutput("out")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$run, {
    session$sendCustomMessage("chunkRun", list(chunkId = CHUNK_ID))
    output$out <- renderPrint({
      exprs <- parse(text = input$code)
      for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) }
    })
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

### `is.na()` — detecting missing values

`NA` ("Not Available") is R's representation of a missing value. `is.na()` returns `TRUE` wherever a value is missing.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c9">
```
```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 230
library(shiny)
CHUNK_ID <- "w2_c9"
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
  textAreaInput("code", "is.na()", value = "x <- c(1, NA, 3, NA, 5)\nis.na(x)       # TRUE where value is missing\n!is.na(x)      # TRUE where value is present\nx[!is.na(x)]  # Keep only non-missing values", width = '100%', height = '100px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),
  verbatimTextOutput("out")
)
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$run, {
    session$sendCustomMessage("chunkRun", list(chunkId = CHUNK_ID))
    output$out <- renderPrint({
      exprs <- parse(text = input$code)
```

### Counting NAs with `sum(is.na())`

Because `TRUE` = 1 and `FALSE` = 0, you can count `NA` values by calling `sum()` on the result of `is.na()`.

### The full cleanup pipeline

Putting it all together — this is the workflow you will apply to the real diabetes dataset in your RStudio exercises.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 330
library(shiny)
CHUNK_ID <- "w2_c14"
DAT <- data.frame(
  age      = c(46, 29, 58, 67, 64, 34),
  chol     = c(203, 165, NA, 259, 294, 155),
  weight   = c(202, NA, 165, 189, 170, 125),
  bp.2s    = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA),

)

  tags$script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
  textAreaInput("code", "Full cleanup", value = "cat('Before:', nrow(dat), 'rows,', ncol(dat), 'cols\\n')\n\n# Step 1: Save original, remove unneeded columns\ndat.original <- dat\ni.remove <- which(colnames(dat) %in% c('bp.2s', 'time.ppn'))\ndat <- dat[, -i.remove]\n\n# Step 2: Remove rows with any NA\nnb_NA <- apply(dat, 1, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))\ndat   <- dat[-which(nb_NA > 0), ]\n\ncat('After: ', nrow(dat), 'rows,', ncol(dat), 'cols\\n')\ndat", width = '100%', height = '170px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),

)

    output$out <- renderPrint({

}
```

### `qqnorm()` + `qqline()` — testing for normality

A **Q-Q plot** compares your data's quantiles to those of a theoretical normal distribution. Points on the diagonal line = data is approximately normal. Deviations = skewness or heavy tails.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c20">
```
```{shinylive-r}

#| viewerHeight: 410

  textAreaInput("code", "qqnorm() + qqline()", value = "bp.1s  <- c(118,110,142,138,180,100,128,132,155,108,135,119,161,122,105,143,127,115,95,168)\nskewed <- c(1,1,2,2,2,3,3,5,8,13,21,34,55,89)\n\npar(mfrow = c(1, 2))\nqqnorm(bp.1s,  main = 'Blood Pressure (normal?)', col='#1a4d1a', pch=16); qqline(bp.1s,  col='#d9534f', lwd=2)\nqqnorm(skewed, main = 'Skewed data',              col='#1a4d1a', pch=16); qqline(skewed, col='#d9534f', lwd=2)", width = '100%', height = '110px'),
  actionButton("run", "Run Code", class = "btn-success"),
```

```{=html}
</div>
<script>
function checkLoadingQuiz() {
  var score = 0, total = 3;
  var l1 = document.querySelector('input[name="l1"]:checked'), l1f = document.getElementById('l1-feedback');
  if (l1 && l1.id === 'l1b') { l1f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! dim() always returns (rows, columns) — rows first!'; l1f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (l1) { l1f.innerHTML = '❌ Not quite. dim() returns c(rows, cols). 400 patients, 17 variables → c(400, 17).'; l1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var l2 = document.querySelector('input[name="l2"]:checked'), l2f = document.getElementById('l2-feedback');
  if (l2 && l2.id === 'l2b') { l2f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! head(dat) shows the first 6 rows. Use head(dat, n) for a custom number.'; l2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (l2) { l2f.innerHTML = '❌ Not right. head() shows the beginning of the data — default is 6 rows.'; l2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var l3 = document.querySelector('input[name="l3"]:checked'), l3f = document.getElementById('l3-feedback');
  if (l3 && l3.id === 'l3b') { l3f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! dat$age is the standard way to access a column by name in R.'; l3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (l3) { l3f.innerHTML = '❌ Try dat$age or dat[, "age"] in the sandbox!'; l3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('loading-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 All correct!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_loading'); }
  else { res.innerHTML = score + ' of ' + total + ' correct. Try again!'; res.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
}
</script>
```

```{shinylive-r}
      exprs <- parse(text=input$code)
      for (e in exprs) { res <- withVisible(eval(e)); if (!is.null(res$value) && res$visible) print(res$value) }
    })
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```{=html}
<script>
function checkCleanupQuiz() {
  var score = 0, total = 3;
  var c1 = document.querySelector('input[name="c1"]:checked'), c1f = document.getElementById('c1-feedback');
  if (c1 && c1.id === 'c1b') { c1f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! which() returns INDICES — try x[which(x > 5)] to get the values.'; c1f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (c1) { c1f.innerHTML = '❌ which() returns positions, not values. Run it in the sandbox!'; c1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var c2 = document.querySelector('input[name="c2"]:checked'), c2f = document.getElementById('c2-feedback');
  if (c2 && c2.id === 'c2b') { c2f.innerHTML = '✅ Right! The comma separates rows (left, empty = all) from columns (right). Negative = exclude.'; c2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (c2) { c2f.innerHTML = '❌ Remember: dat[rows, columns]. To select columns use dat[, ...]. Negative index removes.'; c2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var c3 = document.querySelector('input[name="c3"]:checked'), c3f = document.getElementById('c3-feedback');
  if (c3 && c3.id === 'c3b') { c3f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! MARGIN=1 means row-wise. Each result value = NA count for one patient.'; c3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (c3) { c3f.innerHTML = '❌ MARGIN=1 applies the function to each row. MARGIN=2 would be column-wise.'; c3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('cleanup-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 All correct!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_cleanup'); }
  else { res.innerHTML = score + ' of ' + total + ' correct. Try again!'; res.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
}
</script>
```

```{=html}
  var score = 0, total = 3;
  var v1 = document.querySelector('input[name="v1"]:checked'), v1f = document.getElementById('v1-feedback');
  if (v1 && v1.id === 'v1b') { v1f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! More breaks = more (narrower) bins. Fewer breaks = broader view.'; v1f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (v1) { v1f.innerHTML = '❌ Try hist(x, breaks=3) vs hist(x, breaks=20) in the sandbox and compare!'; v1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var v2 = document.querySelector('input[name="v2"]:checked'), v2f = document.getElementById('v2-feedback');
  if (v2 && v2.id === 'v2b') { v2f.innerHTML = '✅ Right! The box spans Q1–Q3 (middle 50%), the line is the median, whiskers extend to 1.5×IQR.'; v2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (v2) { v2f.innerHTML = '❌ The central line in a boxplot is always the median — not the mean!'; v2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var v3 = document.querySelector('input[name="v3"]:checked'), v3f = document.getElementById('v3-feedback');
  if (v3 && v3.id === 'v3c') { v3f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! Points on the diagonal = matches the normal distribution. Curves away = skewed or heavy tails.'; v3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (v3) { v3f.innerHTML = '❌ A Q-Q plot compares your data\'s quantiles to a theoretical distribution (usually normal).'; v3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('viz-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 All correct!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_viz'); }
  else { res.innerHTML = score + ' of ' + total + ' correct. Try again!'; res.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
}
</script>
```

```{=html}
  else if (e1) { e1f.innerHTML = '❌ hist() makes bars. density() makes a smooth curve — pass its result to plot().'; e1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var e2 = document.querySelector('input[name="e2"]:checked'), e2f = document.getElementById('e2-feedback');
  if (e2 && e2.id === 'e2b') { e2f.innerHTML = '✅ Right! Negative row index removes those rows. dat[-i.missing, ] keeps everyone else.'; e2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (e2) { e2f.innerHTML = '❌ dat[i.missing, ] would KEEP those rows. Add a - to REMOVE them: dat[-i.missing, ].'; e2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var e3 = document.querySelector('input[name="e3"]:checked'), e3f = document.getElementById('e3-feedback');
  if (e3 && e3.id === 'e3b') { e3f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! c("a","b","c") %in% c("b","d") → c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE). Useful for finding columns by name.'; e3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (e3) { e3f.innerHTML = '❌ %in% tests membership — TRUE if the element appears anywhere in the right-hand vector.'; e3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('exercise-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 Week 2 complete — excellent work!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_exercises'); }
```

## 1 – Loading and Exploring Data

When you receive a dataset for the first time, your first goal is to **understand its structure** before doing any analysis.

### `head()` and `tail()` — your first look

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c1">
```
```{shinylive-python}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 340
from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive
import io, contextlib, ast, pandas as pd

CHUNK_ID = "w2_c1"
DAT = pd.DataFrame({
    'age':    [46,29,58,67,64,34,30,37],
    'gender': ["female","female","female","male","male","female","male","male"],
    'chol':   [203,165,228,259,294,155,170,205],
    'weight': [202,122,165,189,170,125,143,156],
    'bp_2s':  [None]*8,
    'location': ["Louisa","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa","Buckingham","Louisa"]
})
app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.tags.script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
    ui.input_text_area("code", "head() / tail()", value="print(dat.head())      # First 5 rows (default)\nprint(dat.head(3))     # First 3 rows\nprint(dat.tail(2))     # Last 2 rows", width='100%', height='80px'),
    ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("out")
)
def server(input, output, session):
    @render.text
    @reactive.event(input.run)
    async def out():
        await session.send_custom_message("chunkRun", {"chunkId": CHUNK_ID})
        f = io.StringIO(); ns = {"dat": DAT.copy(), "pd": pd}
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(f):
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(input.code())
                for node in tree.body:
                    if isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
                        val = eval(compile(ast.Expression(node.value),'<s>','eval'), ns)
                        if val is not None: print(val)
                    else: exec(compile(ast.Module([node],[]),'<s>','exec'), ns)
            except Exception as e: print(f"Error: {e}")
        return f.getvalue()
app = App(app_ui, server)
```

```{=html}
</div>
```

### `df.describe()` — a full statistical overview

`describe()` shows count, mean, std, min, quartiles, and max for numeric columns. Notice that the `count` for `glyhb` is 7 instead of 8 — that's because one value is missing (`NaN`).

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c4">
```

## 2 – Data Cleanup

Raw data is rarely analysis-ready. You typically need to remove irrelevant columns, handle missing values (`NaN`), and reorder variables. Four tools are essential for this: `np.where()`, `isin()`, `isna()`, and `apply()` / `isna().sum(axis=1)`.

### `np.where()` — finding positions

`np.where(condition)` returns the **indices** (positions) where the condition is `True` — not the values themselves. It is the Python equivalent of R's `which()`.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c7">
```
```{shinylive-python}

#| viewerHeight: 260

    ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("out")
)

                        if val is not None: print(val)
                    else: exec(compile(ast.Module([node],[]),'<s>','exec'), ns)
            except Exception as e: print(f"Error: {e}")
        return f.getvalue()
```

### `isin()` — testing membership

`isin()` checks whether each element of a Series appears in a given list. It is the Python equivalent of R's `%in%`.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c8">
```

### `isna()` — detecting missing values

`NaN` ("Not a Number") is Python's representation of a missing value. `pd.isna()` returns `True` wherever a value is missing.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c9">
```

### `apply()` — applying a function to every row or column

`df.apply(func, axis=...)` applies a function to every row (`axis=1`) or column (`axis=0`). Note: in pandas `axis=0` means column-wise and `axis=1` means row-wise — the opposite of R's `MARGIN`.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c12">
```

## 3 – Visualising Data

Once the data is clean, visualisation helps you understand **distributions**, **outliers**, and **relationships** between variables. Python uses `matplotlib` for plotting.

### `plt.hist()` — histograms

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c15">
```
```{shinylive-python}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 410
from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

CHUNK_ID = "w2_c15"
app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.tags.script('Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler("chunkRun",function(m){window.parent.postMessage({type:"chunkDone",chunkId:m.chunkId},"*");});'),
    ui.input_text_area("code", "plt.hist()", value="import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nstab_glu = [87,97,105,90,200,82,91,107,139,95,\n            112,88,145,97,83,125,110,93,78,155]\nplt.hist(stab_glu,\n         color='#a8d5a2', edgecolor='white')\nplt.title('Stabilized Glucose')\nplt.xlabel('Glucose concentration')", width='100%', height='120px'),
    ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"),
    ui.output_plot("plot", height="220px")
)
def server(input, output, session):
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.run)
    async def _notify():
        await session.send_custom_message("chunkRun", {"chunkId": CHUNK_ID})
    @render.plot
    @reactive.event(input.run)
    def plot():
        plt.clf()
        ns = {"plt": plt, "np": np}
        try:
            exec(input.code(), ns)
        except Exception as e:
            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
            ax.text(0.5, 0.5, f"Error: {e}", ha='center', va='center', transform=ax.transAxes, color='red')
        return plt.gcf()
app = App(app_ui, server)
```
```{=html}
</div>
```

### Controlling bin width with `bins`

More `bins` = more (narrower) bars = more detail. Fewer = less detail. Try different values to see the effect.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c16">
```

### `scipy.stats.probplot()` — testing for normality (QQ-plots)

A **Q-Q plot** compares your data's quantiles to a theoretical normal distribution. Points on the diagonal = approximately normal. Deviations = skewness or heavy tails.

```{=html}
<div class="chunk-track" data-chunk-id="w2_c20">
```

```{shinylive-python}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 240
from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive
import io, contextlib, ast, pandas as pd

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_text_area("code", "Sandbox", value="import pandas as pd\ndat = pd.DataFrame({'age':[46,29,58,67,64],'gender':['f','f','f','m','m'],'chol':[203,165,228,259,294]})\n# Try: dat.shape, dat.head(), dat.describe(), dat.columns ...", width='100%', height='100px'),
    ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("out")
)
def server(input, output, session):
    @render.text
    @reactive.event(input.run)
    def out():
        f = io.StringIO(); ns = {"pd": pd}
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(f):
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(input.code())
                for node in tree.body:
                    if isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
                        val = eval(compile(ast.Expression(node.value),'<s>','eval'), ns)
                        if val is not None: print(val)
                    else: exec(compile(ast.Module([node],[]),'<s>','exec'), ns)
            except Exception as e: print(f"Error: {e}")
        return f.getvalue()
app = App(app_ui, server)
```

```{=html}
<script>
function checkPyLoadingQuiz() {
  var score = 0, total = 3;
  var pl1 = document.querySelector('input[name="pl1"]:checked'), pl1f = document.getElementById('pl1-feedback');
  if (pl1 && pl1.id === 'pl1b') { pl1f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! df.shape always returns (rows, columns) — rows first!'; pl1f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pl1) { pl1f.innerHTML = '❌ Not quite. df.shape returns (rows, cols). 400 patients, 17 variables → (400, 17).'; pl1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var pl2 = document.querySelector('input[name="pl2"]:checked'), pl2f = document.getElementById('pl2-feedback');
  if (pl2 && pl2.id === 'pl2b') { pl2f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! df.head() shows the first 5 rows by default (not 6 like in R!). Use df.head(n) for a custom number.'; pl2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pl2) { pl2f.innerHTML = '❌ Not right. head() shows the beginning of the data — default is 5 rows in pandas.'; pl2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var pl3 = document.querySelector('input[name="pl3"]:checked'), pl3f = document.getElementById('pl3-feedback');
  if (pl3 && pl3.id === 'pl3b') { pl3f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! df[\'age\'] is the standard way to access a column by name in pandas.'; pl3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pl3) { pl3f.innerHTML = '❌ Try df[\'age\'] or df.age in the sandbox!'; pl3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('py-loading-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 All correct!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_loading'); }
  else { res.innerHTML = score + ' of ' + total + ' correct. Try again!'; res.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
}
</script>
```

```{=html}
  if (pc1 && pc1.id === 'pc1b') { pc1f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! np.where() returns a tuple of arrays with INDICES — use x[x > 5] to get the values directly.'; pc1f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }

  if (pc2 && pc2.id === 'pc2b') { pc2f.innerHTML = '✅ Right! df.drop(columns=[...]) is the clean pandas way to remove columns by name.'; pc2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pc2) { pc2f.innerHTML = '❌ Use df.drop(columns=[\'bp_2s\', \'time_ppn\']) to remove columns by name.'; pc2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var pc3 = document.querySelector('input[name="pc3"]:checked'), pc3f = document.getElementById('pc3-feedback');
  if (pc3 && pc3.id === 'pc3b') { pc3f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! axis=1 means row-wise. Each result value = NaN count for one patient (row).'; pc3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pc3) { pc3f.innerHTML = '❌ axis=1 applies across columns → one result per row. Use axis=0 for column-wise.'; pc3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('py-cleanup-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 All correct!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_cleanup'); }
  else { res.innerHTML = score + ' of ' + total + ' correct. Try again!'; res.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
}
```

```{shinylive-python}
def server(input, output, session):
    @render.plot
    @reactive.event(input.run)
    def plot():
        plt.clf()
        ns = {"plt": plt}
        try:
            exec(input.code(), ns)
        except Exception as e:
            fig, ax = plt.subplots()
            ax.text(0.5, 0.5, f"Error: {e}", ha='center', va='center', transform=ax.transAxes, color='red')
        return plt.gcf()
app = App(app_ui, server)
```

```{=html}
<script>
function checkPyVizQuiz() {
  var score = 0, total = 3;
  var pv1 = document.querySelector('input[name="pv1"]:checked'), pv1f = document.getElementById('pv1-feedback');
  if (pv1 && pv1.id === 'pv1b') { pv1f.innerHTML = '✅ Correct! More bins = more (narrower) bars. Fewer bins = broader view.'; pv1f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pv1) { pv1f.innerHTML = '❌ Try plt.hist(x, bins=3) vs plt.hist(x, bins=20) in the sandbox and compare!'; pv1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var pv2 = document.querySelector('input[name="pv2"]:checked'), pv2f = document.getElementById('pv2-feedback');
  if (pv2 && pv2.id === 'pv2b') { pv2f.innerHTML = '✅ Right! The box spans Q1–Q3 (middle 50%), the line is the median, whiskers extend to 1.5×IQR.'; pv2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pv2) { pv2f.innerHTML = '❌ The central line in a boxplot is always the median — not the mean!'; pv2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var pv3 = document.querySelector('input[name="pv3"]:checked'), pv3f = document.getElementById('pv3-feedback');
  if (pv3 && pv3.id === 'pv3c') { pv3f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! Points on the diagonal = matches the normal distribution. Curves away = skewed or heavy tails.'; pv3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pv3) { pv3f.innerHTML = '❌ A Q-Q plot compares your data\'s quantiles to a theoretical distribution (usually normal).'; pv3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('py-viz-result');
  if (score === total) { res.innerHTML = '🎉 All correct!'; res.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; markQuizDone('w2_q_viz'); }
  else { res.innerHTML = score + ' of ' + total + ' correct. Try again!'; res.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
}
</script>
```

```{shinylive-python}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 240
from shiny import App, ui, render, reactive
import io, contextlib, ast, pandas as pd

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_text_area("code", "Sandbox", value="import pandas as pd\n# Try combining the tools you've learned!\ndat = pd.DataFrame({'a':[1,None,3], 'b':['x','y',None]})\nnb_NA = dat.isna().sum(axis=1)\nprint(dat[nb_NA == 0])", width='100%', height='100px'),
    ui.input_action_button("run", "Run Code", class_="btn-success"),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("out")
)
def server(input, output, session):
    @render.text
    @reactive.event(input.run)
    def out():
        f = io.StringIO(); ns = {"pd": pd}
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(f):
            try:
                tree = ast.parse(input.code())
                for node in tree.body:
                    if isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
                        val = eval(compile(ast.Expression(node.value),'<s>','eval'), ns)
                        if val is not None: print(val)
                    else: exec(compile(ast.Module([node],[]),'<s>','exec'), ns)
            except Exception as e: print(f"Error: {e}")
        return f.getvalue()
app = App(app_ui, server)
```

```{=html}
function checkPyExerciseQuiz() {
  var score = 0, total = 3;
  var pe1 = document.querySelector('input[name="pe1"]:checked'), pe1f = document.getElementById('pe1-feedback');

  else if (pe1) { pe1f.innerHTML = '❌ plt.hist() makes bars. Use scipy.stats.gaussian_kde() for a smooth density curve.'; pe1f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }

  if (pe2 && pe2.id === 'pe2b') { pe2f.innerHTML = '✅ Right! The ~ operator inverts a boolean mask. df[~i_missing] keeps all rows that do NOT have NaNs.'; pe2f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pe2) { pe2f.innerHTML = '❌ df[i_missing] would KEEP those rows. Use ~ to invert: df[~i_missing]. Or simply df.dropna().'; pe2f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var pe3 = document.querySelector('input[name="pe3"]:checked'), pe3f = document.getElementById('pe3-feedback');
  if (pe3 && pe3.id === 'pe3b') { pe3f.innerHTML = '✅ Exactly! pd.Series([\'a\',\'b\',\'c\']).isin([\'b\',\'d\']) → [False, True, False]. Very useful for filtering columns by name.'; pe3f.style.color = '#1a4d1a'; score++; }
  else if (pe3) { pe3f.innerHTML = '❌ isin() tests membership — True if the element appears in the given list.'; pe3f.style.color = '#d9534f'; }
  var res = document.getElementById('py-exercise-result');

}
</script>
```
